text: E1b-01 closing. audit-E1/section-01.md written (part 1 of the audit's section 1: the quotes and ids against the logs, the quotes against the raw record, the store's figures, the clocks), with seven new scripts in audit-E1/, each with its output; notes-E1.md section E1b-01 written; 8 defects lines appended (109 lines). No .pause. Next: done.sh E1; then E1b-02, the orderings, the counts, coverage and the canvas.

E1b-02 opened. Orderings, from orderings.py (E1a) and prior_sections.py (written and run now, output prior_sections.json). (1) The scheme frozen before B3's first batch: held. scheme_final.jsonl has two hashes in all snaps: fb8b543a9898 at B2b-r3-p3's close (12 Oct 12:43:18Z), then 4b471d29dd41 from B2c's packets-out (13:10:24Z) in 541 snaps to now; B3's first fleet call was at 15:17:38Z. (2) prior.md sections 1 to 6 sealed before B1's first theme_discovery.jsonl line: held, proved by rebuilding the file from the transcripts' writes. A Write (7 Oct 13:13:59Z) and an Edit (13:15:03Z) at B1a give sha 7aa5240047ce, the hash of 321 snaps from B1a's close (13:16:39Z) to C5; the first theme_discovery line is at 13:56:08. Two Edits at D1a (15 Oct 15:56Z) give 720068eeaf87, the file as it stands. Section by section, the preamble and sections 1 to 6 are byte for byte the same then and now; only sections 7 and 8 changed, from one placeholder to their text. No Bash command wrote prior.md. (3) Sections 7 and 8 sealed at D1 before DROPS/D was ingested: held; the sealed hash is first snapped at D1a's packets-out (15 Oct 19:44:16Z) and the first snap that lists adaptations.jsonl is D2a's adaptations-in (16 Oct 10:17:19Z). (4) The model hashed at C5's close before D1: held; e15f96470271 at C5c-13's close (15 Oct 14:42:06Z), D1's first snap at 19:44:16Z. The model moved after, at D3, to 46384686d617, which is the file now and at D6: the return's rulings, moves 172 to 197, declared as amendments.

E1b-02 orderings, continued, from snap_order.py (written and run now, output snap_order.json). (5) Every D4 move snapped before the projection and the chunk-share tree: held for the branch cuts, as QE1-001's answer frames it. 34 D4 move snaps changed branches.jsonl from the snap before (moves 201 to 236); the last, D4-move-merging-236, is at 25 Oct 16:21:31Z, and the first snap that lists the projection is D4a-03's interview cut at 19:16:07Z. 82 D4 snaps list the projection or the chunk-share files, and none changed branches.jsonl: they are the room forms made after the projection by J's ruling (moves 238 to 313 and the closes of D4a-03 to D4a-08), not a recut. branches.jsonl as it stands equals its last D4 snap. (6) Every move snap at C2 to D3: held. 198 move snaps carry the numbers 1 to 197, none missing; sorted by number they are sorted by time, but for one pair: D3-move-181-1 (21 Oct 09:31:59Z) is a second snap of move 181's state, 24 seconds before D3-move-developing-181 (09:32:23Z); the diary named it as wrongly named and unused at D3a-53. (7) Every D6 proposal: the 11 lines of proposals-D6.jsonl are all status unvalidated on base 46384686d617, the D3 freeze; amendments-D6.jsonl holds 0 lines. The file has 6 hashes in 19 D6 snaps, each change at the leg its new lines name (D6a-01 to D6a-07), and it is unchanged from D6a-07's close to D6a-18's. A hash shows the file, not each line, so that the earlier lines stayed as written is self-reported. Every other claim about the order of the work is self-reported.

E1b-02 the counts rule. (a) The census twice (counts_rule.py, E1a): 705 rooms in package/store/rooms.jsonl and 705 room folders with a case account, the same set; dropped.jsonl holds 0 lines, so no drop and no reason; counts.py: analysed 705. (b) Stage D4 section 4's four counts: 476 in a branch + 0 unadapted + 229 in no branch + 0 unreturned = 705, n_analysed. (c) The head's ledger figures, as the head stands now (counts_phrases.py): all 7 agree (adjudications 96,568; verdicts 1,029; tier history 1,026; model history 182; findings 45; elements 45; arrows 21). E1a's counts_rule.json read the head before E1a's own Edit, so its 1,020 against 1,026 is no longer true. (d) The 361 count phrases of the 18 handbacks: counts_phrases.py sets aside 26 numbers followed by a comma and 6 decimals (its first run took any comma into the number and set aside none; kept as .superseded-1), leaving 329 counts; a seeded sample of 2 per handback, 36, checked by counts_sample_check.py (two faults of mine fixed, a key B3's defects lack and the re-check verdicts keyed by the readers' own spelling of the room; outputs kept as .superseded-1 and -2) and by hand. 27 recompute and agree (one, handback-A1's 7 defects lines, became 8 later in A1, as the same handback's line 72 says); 4 agree with a stated parameter or list (500 shuffles is c2_arrow_evidence.py's default; 6 items is field-C4.md's list 3; the figure's 20 arrows are figure-C5.md's 20, A21 not drawn); 3 rest on a judgment by hand that no file lets me recompute (A1's 79 of 100, C4's 78 rooms, D3's 48 rooms); 2 disagree with their governing file. handback-B1.md line 20 says 107 episode lines; notes-B1.md line 3108 (B2) counts 106 (line, kind) pairs over 81 lines, and the handback was never corrected. handback-C5-p14.md line 45 says the model's history holds 31 lines (12 element, 12 arrow, 5 condition, 1 role, 1 claim); model/history.jsonl holds 45 C5 lines to pass 14's leg C5c-11 (16, 21, 5, 1, 2) and 30 distinct ids (12, 13, 2, 1, 2), so 31 matches neither. 293 counts were not checked.

E1b-02 coverage (coverage.py, E1a, read now). Rooms read whole, from the read logs, one record per read: every one of the 705 analysed rooms was read by mem.py room, by mem.py forest and through its case account in some log; no room is unread. Forests read whole: 704. The one short is r/COSI, whose forest was read once at A1 from line 11 to 18 of 18: the 10 header lines were skipped and every tree line read. By log (a log names the log that was open, not the stage the reading served): A1 room 1,936 reads of 705 rooms, forest 205 of 155, case 887 of 705; B1 room 1,873 of 705, forest 305 of 110 (all whole); C2 room 343 of 67, forest 498 of 67; C5 room 261 of 218, forest 32 of 32; D3 forest 14,054 reads of 703 rooms, all whole, and 77,047 cite reads over 705; D5 room 10 of 8; D6 case 77 of 40. B2, B3, B4, D1, D2 and D4 read no room by mem.py, which is no gap: the fleets read for them and leave no read log (their reading is in _fleet_raw: B3 1,223 entries, D2v 708, D3v 708, B4 51 and B4-openai-astra 55, C2 the reviewer, C5 the three readers; DROPS/D holds 706 room entries).

E1b-02 rule 7's uses of the canvas, stage by stage (canvas_uses.py, E1a, then by hand). A1: mem.py room with the canvas 715 reads and mem.py canvas 722 calls over 705 rooms, for the made line, declared (departures line 5). B1 1,874, C2 22 (19 rooms), C5 218, D3 4 and D5 5 room reads showed the canvas, which rule 7 allows; the record names no reading, placement, cut, name or element these shaped, and whether any was shaped cannot be told from the logs: self-reported. D4: the projection came after the branch cuts (ordering 5); the 75 D4 tier history grounds that name the canvas all say no canvas field was used. D5: two mem.py canvas calls at D5a-40 and D5b and the canvas fields of branches-D5.jsonl, all in survival-D5.md's reading after the record, declared. D6: d6b_survival_forms.py reads survival from the record, and notes-D6 says the canvas is not read. No element, arrow, proposition, finding or branch carries a canvas figure: the passages that name the atlas, artwork or survival are members' own acts or the coded record (P12's atlas entries, A05's quote, F-021's bound saying the canvas is not evidence, F-023, F-027, F17, F18). No undeclared use found. For a reader to look: elements argued mostly from what rooms kept (P12, P13, P22, A09; the account's survival paragraph, defects line 100); branch names that say what rooms did with their work (F09, F12, F17, F18, F23, F32); and the six room forms, cut with the projection in the folder (the 82 snaps of QE1-001).

E1b-02 defects.jsonl: 2 lines appended by out/_analysis/e1b02_defects_lines.py, the two handback counts that disagree with their governing files (handback-B1.md line 20, 107 for 106 over 81 lines; handback-C5-p14.md line 45, 31 history lines for 45 lines or 30 ids). The ledger holds 111 lines, 10 of them E1's.
